They noticed an impossible anomaly hidden deep inside their data. They were studying absolutely enormous deposits of ancient sandstone spread across the southern continents. When the crystal originally forms inside cooling magma deep within the Earth, its specific atomic structure eagerly allows uranium atoms to enter, but it completely rejects lead atoms because lead atoms are simply the wrong size to fit. Matching these precise fingerprints across five heavily separated continents could only mean one incredibly terrifying thing. Normally, every region has its own unique geological history, so its sand carries a unique mix of ages. But the Trans Gondwanan Supermountain faced an even more brutal reality. When it stood, there were absolutely no plants on land. No root systems existed to hold the soil together.
